title: Simple sorts
description:
Write the two simple sorts as templates that take a comparator, plus a measure of disorder:

```cpp
template <class T, class Less = std::less<T>> long long insertionSort(std::vector<T>& a, Less less = Less{});   // returns the number of shifts
template <class T, class Less = std::less<T>> void selectionSort(std::vector<T>& a, Less less = Less{});
template <class T, class Less = std::less<T>> bool isSorted(const std::vector<T>& a, Less less = Less{});
long long countInversionsSlow(const std::vector<int>& a);      // pairs i < j with a[i] > a[j], by checking every pair
```

- `insertionSort` must be **stable** (never move an element past an equal one) and return how many times it moved an element one place to the right. That number always equals the number of inversions.
- `isSorted` is true when no element is `less` than the one before it. An empty vector is sorted.
- Use only `less(a, b)` to compare: the tests sort with comparators that order by one field only.
hints: For stability, keep shifting only while the value is **strictly** less than its left neighbour: `while (j > 0 && less(value, a[j - 1]))`. Stopping at an equal element keeps the earlier one first.
